correctness.rationale: Let λ be feasible, (q,z) its center and k=1−t. The reflected upper generator forces (1+λ)z≥1; the reflected lower generator, at target height (1+λ)z, fits into [λ−k(1+λ)z]B. The base asymmetry definition makes this factor at least σ=s(B), so λ≥σ+k. For c∈M(B), choose z=1/(σ+2−t), q=(σ+1)c/(σ+2−t); one generator follows from optimal base reflection and the other from convexity of B plus c∈B, proving equality for arbitrary nonsymmetric B without assuming 0∈B. Equality locks axial z when t<1; t=1 is the Cartesian product and admits the stated interval. Exact rational generator checks for triangular base at five t values independently corroborated. The classical base bound 1≤σ≤m yields sharp equality classes.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a natural universal affine-geometric transformation rule for all convex bases, including nonsmooth asymmetric ones; the exact optimal center loci and dimension jump at t=1 are structural and not a cosmetic substitution into dimension bounds. Researchers studying asymmetry of cones, frusta or convex interpolations can use the precise base-to-frustum law.
residual_risks: The assessed value is limited to the precise natural family and invariant in the final claim, not any unstated generalization.

final_claim: For any compact m-dimensional convex base B (m≥1) and 0≤t≤1, F_t(B)=conv(B×{0},tB×{1}) has exact Minkowski asymmetry s(F_t)=s(B)+1−t. For t<1 every minimizing reflection center has z=1/[s(B)+2−t] and horizontal coordinate (s(B)+1)c/[s(B)+2−t] for c∈M(B); at t=1 centers equal M(B)×[1/(s(B)+1),s(B)/(s(B)+1)].
